description: Statistics for biology, medicine and public health: study design, describing biological and clinical data, probability distributions in health data, estimation and hypothesis testing, regression for continuous, binary and count outcomes, survival analysis and the problem of multiple testing in genomic studies. Every method is computed by hand on small examples, then run on real health datasets with interactive plots and notebooks in the browser, taught to the depth of a strong biostatistics course for computing and health science students.
modelledOn: Kirkwood and Sterne, Essential Medical Statistics
Pagano and Gauvreau, Principles of Biostatistics
Altman, Practical Statistics for Medical Research
outcomes: Choose an appropriate study design for a biological or medical question and identify bias, confounding and sources of error.
Summarise and visualise biological and clinical data and compute measures of disease frequency and association.
Apply probability distributions to model counts, proportions and measurements in health data, and evaluate diagnostic tests.
Estimate parameters with confidence intervals and carry out and interpret hypothesis tests, including power and sample size calculations.
Fit, check and interpret linear, logistic and Poisson regression models and Kaplan-Meier and Cox survival models.
Control error rates when testing many hypotheses and report analyses reproducibly according to reporting guidelines.

units.title: Study design in biology and medicine
topics: Populations, samples and variables; observational and experimental studies
Cross-sectional surveys, case-control and cohort studies; randomised controlled trials, blinding and allocation concealment
Bias, confounding and effect modification; causation and the Bradford Hill considerations
Sampling methods: simple random, stratified, cluster and multistage designs as used in demographic and health surveys
Ethics of research on people: informed consent, ethics committees, the Declaration of Helsinki; CONSORT and STROBE reporting guidelines

units.title: Describing biological data
topics: Types of data: categorical, ordinal, discrete and continuous; data cleaning and missing values
Measures of location and spread; percentiles and growth reference charts for children
Graphs: histograms, box plots, scatter plots, Kaplan-Meier curves, forest plots
Measures of disease frequency: prevalence, incidence rate, cumulative incidence; malaria incidence by district
Measures of association: risk difference, risk ratio, odds ratio, rate ratio

units.title: Probability distributions in health data
topics: Probability rules, conditional probability and Bayes' theorem
Diagnostic tests: sensitivity, specificity, predictive values, likelihood ratios and ROC curves; malaria rapid diagnostic tests against microscopy
Binomial distribution for proportions such as sickle cell trait carriers; Poisson distribution for counts of cases
The normal distribution, standardisation and the central limit theorem; transformations of skewed data
Simulation of sampling distributions in the browser

units.title: Estimation and hypothesis testing
topics: Standard errors and confidence intervals for means, proportions, differences and ratios
Hypothesis tests and p-values; type I and type II errors; statistical versus clinical significance
t-tests, paired tests and their non-parametric counterparts: Wilcoxon and Mann-Whitney
Chi-squared and Fisher's exact tests for contingency tables; McNemar's test
Analysis of variance and post hoc comparisons
Power and sample size calculations for a trial of a new antimalarial

units.title: Regression for health outcomes
topics: Correlation and simple linear regression; least squares, residuals and model checking
Multiple linear regression: adjusting for confounders, interactions, categorical predictors
Logistic regression for binary outcomes; interpreting odds ratios; risk factors for anaemia in pregnancy
Poisson and negative binomial regression for counts and rates; offsets
Model building, collinearity and overfitting; prediction models and their validation
Clustered and repeated measures data in brief: mixed models and generalised estimating equations

units.title: Survival analysis
topics: Time-to-event data, censoring and truncation; survival and hazard functions
Kaplan-Meier estimation and the log-rank test
Cox proportional hazards regression; hazard ratios; checking proportional hazards
Time-varying covariates and competing risks in brief
Survival of patients on antiretroviral therapy or of children with sickle cell disease in a cohort study

units.title: Multiple testing
topics: Why testing many hypotheses inflates false positives; the family-wise error rate
Bonferroni and Holm corrections; false discovery rate and the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure
Genome-wide association studies: significance thresholds, Manhattan and QQ plots, population structure
Differential expression analysis and q-values; subgroup analyses and p-hacking in clinical research

units.title: Bayesian methods and reproducible analysis
topics: Bayesian inference in brief: priors, posteriors and credible intervals for a prevalence estimate
Meta-analysis: fixed and random effects, heterogeneity and forest plots
Reproducible analysis with scripts and notebooks; data protection for health records
Capstone: a complete analysis of a public health dataset with a statistical analysis plan and report
